subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Russian Samovar Tradition
description: A 60-second lesson on Russian Samovar Tradition.

hook.text: The Russian samovar—a heated metal urn—once sat at the center of every Russian household as both heater and teapot.

buildup.text: A concentrated tea brew (zavarka) sits on top. You pour a little into your cup and dilute with hot water from the spigot.

discovery.text: The samovar doubled as a room heater. In brutal Russian winters, it warmed both the tea and the family around it.

twist.text: Russian tea is traditionally served with jam (varenye) spooned into the cup or eaten from a saucer between sips.

climax.text: Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, and Chekhov all wrote scenes around samovars. It was Russian domestic life's central object.

punchline.text: The samovar warmed the room, brewed the tea, and held the family together.

quiz.question: What is 'zavarka' in Russian tea tradition?
options: A concentrated tea brew diluted with hot water from the samovar
